hypotheses.justification: This follows from `hA : IsSelfAdjoint A` by the Mathlib lemma `IsSelfAdjoint.dense_domain` (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/LinearPMap.lean): if the domain were not dense, the junk value of `A†` would have domain ⊤, which is dense, a contradiction. `hAdense` is used only to fill the `A_dense` field of the problem record. Without it, fill that field with `hA.dense_domain`; the rest of the proof does not change. The library already uses this lemma (Unbounded/Core.lean says these hypotheses are derivable). Each of `hAdense`, `hAclosed`, `hA0dense` and `hA0closed` can be deleted on its own, and all four can also be deleted together.

This follows from `hA` by the Mathlib lemma `IsSelfAdjoint.isClosed`: every self-adjoint `LinearPMap` is closed. The lemma needs `[CompleteSpace ER]`, which is available. `hAclosed` is used only to fill the `A_closed` field. Without it, fill that field with `hA.isClosed`; the rest of the proof does not change.

This follows from `hA0 : IsSelfAdjoint A0` by `IsSelfAdjoint.dense_domain`. It is used only to fill the `A₀_dense` field. Without it, fill that field with `hA0.dense_domain`; the rest of the proof does not change.

This follows from `hA0` by `IsSelfAdjoint.isClosed`. The lemma needs `[CompleteSpace FR]`, which is available. `hA0closed` is used only to fill the `A₀_closed` field. Without it, fill that field with `hA0.isClosed`; the rest of the proof does not change.
